questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The decision for studying in Barcelona was made because of the city. It has so many things to offer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy and the exchange office in Barcelona were helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive the e-mails that other students received and the exchange office were quick to respond and resolve the issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that easy. We lived four guys together - which I guess made it more difficult to find housing. I would go through Idealista or AirBNB.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Not the cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty expensive rent.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty much all done online from home. At the master's level, it was kind of confusing to know what courses that was available or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Relatively fast to answer e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a Master's student on economics, know that they are doing trimester structure, meaning that if you expect to do 30 ects in the fall, for example, you are doing a bit more than the intended workload, which is 20.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level wasn't that high but the workload was high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More similar to high school - not the level, but the way of teaching - small classes with participation being important.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Governments and Markets
Economic Growth II
Cooperative Decision-Making and Social Choice
Regional and Urban Economics
Public Economics: Political Economy
Public Policy Analysis and Evaluation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Difficult to say as I didn't really 'enjoy' any of the courses. Maybe Cooperative Decision-Making or Regional and Urban Economics because they were more tangible. Consider doing courses in other faculties instead of the ones in Economics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The agency fee for renting the apartment. Basically a month's rent is spent on the agency to do the contract with the landlord. This can be avoided, I think, if you rent through airbnb, instead of finding an agency through idealista.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Well, maybe we overpaid on the rent. But it was a very nice apartment.
Food and wine were less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe there was some sports available but I never really found out how to apply.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel around Spain to see other cities. Go out to eat and drink in Barcelona.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Same as above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialize that much with local students. it was primarily other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No big challenges

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid-back-ness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you are an economics master's student, do consider whether or not the master's programme is the right for you. A high workload is followed from them doing a trimester and you essentially needing to do a semester worth of ECTS. Not that much flexibility in choosing courses from other faculties because they grade attendance as well, and the faculties do not coordinate. Not that interesting courses available, in my view.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If UAB is a possibility to do exchange maybe consider that instead as most other students from nordic countries choose this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships and experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes a high workload meant not spending time doing more fun things.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
